statement: A survey asked $240$ students to name their favorite season. One quarter of them chose summer, $20\%$ chose winter, $15\%$ chose spring, and everyone else chose autumn. How many students chose autumn?

choices.misconception: I worked out that 40 percent chose autumn and gave 40 as the number of students instead of finding 40 percent of 240.
I forgot to subtract the spring students, so I used 100 - 25 - 20 = 55 percent, and 55 percent of 240 is 132.
I found the students who did not choose autumn, 25 + 20 + 15 = 60 percent of 240 = 144, instead of the ones who did.
I forgot to subtract summer because it was given as a fraction, so I used 100 - 20 - 15 = 65 percent, and 65 percent of 240 is 156.

hints: Write every group as a percent of the whole survey.
One quarter is $25\%$. The autumn percent is whatever is left of $100\%$. Then take that percent of $240$.

solutions.reliable: One quarter is $25\%$. The autumn group is $100\% - 25\% - 20\% - 15\% = 40\%$ of the students. So $0.40 \cdot 240 = 96$ students chose autumn.
solutions.elegant: Count the other groups directly: summer $\frac{240}{4} = 60$, winter $0.2 \cdot 240 = 48$, spring $0.15 \cdot 240 = 36$. Autumn is $240 - 60 - 48 - 36 = 96$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
